clue.text: Funnel cash, primarily to get gold lace

indicators.note: primarily asks for the opening letter of the word cash

parts.note: OR is the heraldic term for gold
net is a fine openwork fabric, a kind of lace

explanation.surface: Someone diverts money mainly into buying gold lace trimmings.
explanation.definitionFit: A cornet is a cone-shaped paper wrapper, the shape of a funnel.

clue.text: Enthusiastic audience left, enthralled by those setting new standards

indicators.note: enthralled by means held inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: to cap is to outdo, so cappers are those who surpass previous standards

explanation.surface: An eager crowd walked out, captivated by trailblazers.
explanation.definitionFit: An appreciative audience applauds, so its members are clapping fans.

clue.text: Desperately desiring seats with good view

indicators.note: desperately suggests wild frantic movement, so the letters of desiring are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone is frantically wanting seats that offer a good view.
explanation.definitionFit: Ringside places are those right next to the boxing ring, giving the best view.

clue.text: Girl's ending up with cream cake

indicators.note: in a down clue up means toward the top, so the final letter of the girl's name moves to the start

parts.note: Claire is a girl's name; the possessive adds no letter

explanation.surface: A girl finally ends up eating a cream cake.
explanation.definitionFit: An eclair is a long choux pastry filled with cream.

clue.text: I produce type of basic meals

parts.note: key means essential or basic, as in a key issue
board means meals provided, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: Someone claims to cook a kind of simple food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I produce type' is the keyboard speaking: pressing its keys produces typed letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressing the keys of a keyboard prints letters, so it could say it makes type.

clue.text: Ignoring all the odds, deb learns style

indicators.note: ignoring the odd-numbered letters leaves only the even ones of deb learns

explanation.surface: A debutante learns style against the odds.
explanation.definitionFit: Elan is dash or flair, a stylish confidence.

clue.text: Animal drug needing money for release

parts.note: a bull is a male bovine animal
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
tin is British slang for money

explanation.surface: An animal needs paying for before it can be set free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'release' is a noun, as in a press release, not a setting free.
explanation.definitionFit: A bulletin is an official statement issued to the public, like a press release.

clue.text: Satisfaction as democrat gets in final words

indicators.note: gets in means enters, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: amen is said at the end of a prayer, so amens are final words

explanation.surface: A democrat has the last word in a dispute and is satisfied.
explanation.definitionFit: Making amends is giving satisfaction or reparation for a wrong.

clue.text: Gloomy, stern, heartless Darcy's around

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one piece wraps the other
heartless means the inner letters of the name are removed, leaving the outside

parts.note: Darcy is the hero of Pride and Prejudice; the possessive stands for is
the stern is the rear of a ship

explanation.surface: Mr Darcy, Jane Austen's hero, is grim, severe and unfeeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' strips the inside of Darcy (Mr Darcy of Pride and Prejudice), leaving its first and last letters, which go around the stern word; 'stern' is a ship's back, not severe.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreary and gloomy both describe something dull and depressing.

clue.text: Registers a new name and drops old

indicators.note: drops means lets fall, so a letter is removed from the word for and

parts.note: also means and, in addition

explanation.surface: A clerk enters a fresh name in the books and strikes out the former one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' looks like a link word but supplies a synonym; 'drops' then removes the letter for 'old' from it.
explanation.definitionFit: Annals are yearly historical records, chronicles kept like a register.

clue.text: Each finding pleasure with the outdated vision — that's sharp

parts.note: glee means delight or pleasure
ye is an archaic spelling of the

explanation.surface: Each person delights in old-fashioned eyesight that turns out to be keen.
explanation.definitionFit: Keen-sighted observation is often called that of an eagle, a bird famed for acute sight.

clue.text: The Spanish upset after game make derisory sounds

indicators.note: after means the reversed article comes after the game

parts.note: whist is a card game

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the Spanish article is read backwards

parts.note: el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Spanish fans, upset after a match, jeer.
explanation.definitionFit: Crowds express scorn with shrill blown notes, so to whistle can be to jeer.

clue.text: Miscellany — it's cheap to organise

indicators.note: organising the letters of it's cheap puts them into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone claims a mixed collection is inexpensive to arrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastiche is a medley of borrowed pieces, a hotchpotch or mixture.

clue.text: Chinese cash backing Red Guard

parts.note: the fen is a small unit of Chinese currency, a hundredth of a yuan

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the word red is read in reverse

explanation.surface: Beijing funds support the Red Guards of the Cultural Revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red Guard' reads as Mao's youth militia; split it, and 'Guard' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A fender is a protective barrier, as on a car wing or a ship's side, so a kind of guard.

clue.text: French very upset about cage for snake

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece encloses the other
in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the French word is read backwards

parts.note: tres is French for very
a pen is an enclosure, a cage

explanation.surface: A Frenchman is very upset about caging a snake.
explanation.definitionFit: A serpent is a literary word for a snake.

clue.text: Reportedly regretted being vulgar

indicators.note: reportedly signals that a word is heard, not seen, so we want something that sounds like a synonym

parts.note: rued means regretted

explanation.surface: Someone was said to be sorry for behaving coarsely.
explanation.definitionFit: Rude and vulgar are synonyms for coarse or offensive behaviour.

clue.text: Hermit's wildly ecstatic, but only the one time

definitions.note: Hermit's is read as hermit is, so the defining noun is hermit

indicators.note: wildly says the letters are thrown about into a new order
but only the one says to keep just one of the two letters standing for time, removing the other

explanation.surface: A recluse is overjoyed, but only on one occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: ECSTATIC has two Ts; 'but only the one time' removes one, leaving ECSATIC, which 'wildly' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascetic is someone living in self-denial, often alone like a recluse.

clue.text: Instrument accompanies "list" recalled for Don Giovanni, perhaps

parts.note: a viol is an early bowed stringed instrument

indicators.note: recalled is read as called back, so the word for list is read backwards

parts.note: a rota is a list of duties

explanation.surface: A string player is accompanied by the famous catalogue aria sung for Don Giovanni.
explanation.walkthrough: In Mozart's opera Leporello sings a 'list' (catalogue) aria of Don Giovanni's conquests; the Don is a seducer and violator of women.
explanation.definitionFit: Don Giovanni is an example of a seducer who abuses women and breaks every rule.

clue.text: Frank's reason for lack of bias

parts.note: frank means candid or open; the possessive is a link
mind can mean reason or intellect

explanation.surface: A man named Frank explains why he is impartial.
explanation.definitionFit: Being receptive to new ideas without prejudice means having no bias.

clue.text: Flustered faltering footless figure

indicators.note: flustered means agitated, so the remaining letters are jumbled
footless means without F, the abbreviation for foot, so that letter is removed

explanation.surface: A nervous speaker stumbles and staggers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'footless' removes F (foot) from FALTERING to leave ALTERING, which 'Flustered' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A triangle is a three-sided geometric figure.

clue.text: Cheers Prince's broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means put out over the air, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: Prince Philip is the royal prince, the late Duke of Edinburgh; with the possessive it is Philip's

explanation.surface: A prince's radio show raises spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheers' is a verb here: fillips are boosts that cheer one up. Prince Philip was the husband of Queen Elizabeth II.
explanation.definitionFit: Fillips are stimuli or boosts that lift the spirits.

clue.text: Fight with weapon missing essential part

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so a letter is removed from the weapon

parts.note: a spear is a pointed throwing weapon
the essential part of a word is its central letter, here the middle of the five-letter weapon

explanation.surface: A combatant fights with a weapon that has lost a vital component.
explanation.definitionFit: To spar is to box or argue, a form of fighting.

clue.text: Soft judge about to return favour

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, soft
ref is short for referee, who judges a game

indicators.note: to return means to come back, so the word for about is read backwards

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A lenient judge returns a favour.
explanation.definitionFit: To prefer is to like better, to favour one over another.

clue.text: Folk see point in most rules for behaviour

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one piece goes into the other
most means nearly all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: ethics are moral principles governing conduct
N is a compass point, north

explanation.surface: People find a point in most codes of conduct.
explanation.definitionFit: Folk, as in folk music or dress, describes traditional culture of a people.

clue.text: Cycling's no good using island beachwear

indicators.note: no means without, so the letter for good is taken out

parts.note: biking means cycling; the possessive is a link

explanation.surface: Cycling is pointless on an island where swimwear is worn.
explanation.definitionFit: A bikini is a two-piece swimsuit worn at the beach.

clue.text: Endless gossip causing upset

indicators.note: endless means both ends are lopped off the word for gossip

parts.note: a prattler is a chatterer, a gossip

explanation.surface: Unceasing tittle-tattle causes distress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gossip' is a person here, a chatterer; 'Endless' trims the first and last letters off PRATTLER.
explanation.definitionFit: To rattle someone is to unnerve or disturb them.

clue.text: Brand model gains in India, at first

indicators.note: at first asks for the opening letter of the word India
model is a verb here, to shape, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A brand's product line makes headway in India early on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'model' looks like a noun after 'Brand' but is a verb, to reshape, signalling the anagram; 'at first' takes only the opening letter of India.
explanation.definitionFit: Insignia are badges or emblems, distinguishing marks like a brand.

clue.text: When in reserves, I'll quit

indicators.note: quit means leave, so the letter is taken out

parts.note: on ice means kept in reserve for later
I'll is read as I will, so the letter I is the one that quits

explanation.surface: A player says they will leave once sent to the reserves.
explanation.definitionFit: Once can mean at the time when, as in once you arrive.

clue.text: Tweak beautiful melody

parts.note: fine can mean beautiful or handsome
a tune is a melody

explanation.surface: Adjust a lovely tune.
explanation.definitionFit: To fine-tune is to make small adjustments, i.e. to tweak.

clue.text: Big shot losing power to Alfred? That's me!

indicators.note: losing means a letter is taken away from the word for big shot

parts.note: a VIP is a very important person, a big shot
P is the physics abbreviation for power
Alfred the Great was an English king

explanation.surface: An important figure loses influence to Alfred, says the setter.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter is Viking, so 'That's me!' defines the answer; Alfred the Great famously fought Viking invaders.
explanation.definitionFit: The setter of this puzzle signs under the pseudonym of a Norse raider.

clue.text: Judge engineers criminal's first summons

parts.note: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

indicators.note: first asks for the opening letter of the word criminal's

parts.note: an order is a command or summons

explanation.surface: A judge sends engineers to issue a criminal's summons.
explanation.walkthrough: In England and Wales a recorder is a part-time judge in the Crown Court.
explanation.definitionFit: A recorder is a barrister or solicitor sitting as a part-time judge.

clue.text: Toy racket

explanation.surface: A plaything is also a bat for tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: To fiddle is to toy idly with something; a fiddle is also a swindle, a racket.
